q: A leader says "saved" after 1 ms, before the follower has the copy. Then the leader crashes. What can be lost, and what is this mode called?
options: Nothing, the follower always has it. Synchronous
The write the client was told about. Asynchronous
Only the oldest data. Synchronous
The follower's disk. Asynchronous
why: With asynchronous replication, "saved" is said before the copy lands. A crash in that gap loses a write the client was promised.

q: Postgres is set to synchronous replication with one follower, and the follower server stops. What happens to the next INSERT on the leader?
options: It succeeds as before
It is refused at once with an error
It waits and does not return, until the follower is back or the wait is cancelled
It is saved only on the follower when it returns
why: In the Postgres test in database lesson 21, the INSERT was still waiting after 2.5 seconds. Sync gives safety, and gives up availability when the follower is gone.

q: N = 3, W = 2, R = 2. A write of v2 reached copies A and B. A read asks B and C, and C still holds v1. What does the read return?
options: v1
v2
An error
Either one, at random
why: The read keeps the answer with the highest version. Any 2 of 3 copies include A or B, so the late copy C cannot win alone.

q: Which settings can give a stale read with N = 3?
options: W = 2 and R = 2
W = 3 and R = 1
W = 2 and R = 1
W = 1 and R = 3
why: With W = 2 and R = 1, R + W is 3, which is not more than N. The write can sit on A and B while the read asks only C. The other three have R + W = 4.

q: N = 3, W = 2, R = 2, and two copies are down. What happens to a write?
options: It succeeds on the one copy that is up
It is refused, because only 1 copy can save it and W is 2
It succeeds and is copied later
It is saved on the copies that are down
why: The store gives up availability to avoid giving a wrong answer. A write needs W saves, and a read needs R answers.

q: A team has 3 copies, all in one data centre, and says "we are safe". What is the problem?
options: 3 copies is too few
Copies in one place can fail together, for example in a power loss
Copies in one place are always out of date
A quorum cannot be made with 3 copies
why: Spread copies across zones, so one failure takes at most one copy.
